org.portico.lrc.services.ownership.data

Class AcquireRequest

  • java.lang.Object
    • org.portico.lrc.services.ownership.data.AcquireRequest
  • All Implemented Interfaces:
    Serializable

    public class AcquireRequest
extends Object
implements Serializable
    This class contains information about any outstanding ownership acquisition requests. It is only intended for internal use by the OwnershipManager.

      • getAttributesUnderAcquisitionRequest

        public Set<Integer> getAttributesUnderAcquisitionRequest(Set<Integer> attributes,
                                                         int federateHandle)
        Considering only those given attributes, find all that are currently under an outstanding ownership acquisition request by the given federate. If there are none, an empty set is returned. Note that this will only return attributes under acquisition request, *NOT* a "requestIfAvailable".

      • getAttributesUnderAcquisitionRequest

        public Map<Integer,Integer> getAttributesUnderAcquisitionRequest(Set<Integer> attributes)
        This method is much like getAttributesUnderAcquisitionRequest(Set, int) except that it will return the attributes that are under an acquisition request from ANY federate. The returned value is a map whose keys are the attribute handles and whose values are the federates that are requesting the ownership assumption. If there are none under outstanding request, an empty map is returned.

      • getAttributesUnderAcquisitionRequest

        public Set<Integer> getAttributesUnderAcquisitionRequest(int federateHandle)
        Returns a set of all the attributes currently under an acquisition request by the federate with the given handle. If there are none, an empty set is returned.

      • updateRequest

        public void updateRequest(Set<Integer> attributes,
                          int federateHandle,
                          AcquireRequest.Status incomingStatus)
        This method will update the local request, recording new information for the specified attributes.

        If the incoming status types are the same, then the associated federate handle for an attribute will only be changed if the incoming handle is LESS than the existing handle.

        If the incoming request is a REQUEST and the existing is REQUEST_AVAILABLE, the existing will be overwritten regardless of the federate handles (R trumps RA in our implementation!)

        If the incoming request is a REQUEST_AVAILABLE and the existing request is a normal REQUEST, no action will be taken as the RA is treated kind of like a "best effort" kind of request.

      • cancelTransfer

        public void cancelTransfer(Set<Integer> attributes)
        This method removes any local trace of the request for ownership transfer for the attributes with the given handles.

      • completeTransfer

        public Set<Integer> completeTransfer(int federateHandle,
                                     boolean ifAvailable)
        This method signals that the federate with the given handle is ending the ownership transfer request. A set of all the attributes it can acquire at this point are returned and the associations for those attributes removed. If there are none available for the identified federate, an empty set is returned.

        If the ifAvailable flag is set to true, only those attributes that were requested as ifAvailable are removed and returned. If it is set to false, only those attributes that have explicitly been released to the federate will be removed and returned. Only those attributes marked as linked to the given federate AND having the same status are considered.

      • releaseAttributes

        public Map<Integer,Integer> releaseAttributes(Set<Integer> attributes)
        This method marks the identified attributes as RELEASED. Attributes remain in this status until the completeTransfer(int, boolean) method is called and the ownership transfer is completed. The returned map contains the attributes as the keys and the handles of the federates as the values. If any of the attributes specified are not under a release request, they are ignored.

      • isAttributeUnderAcquisitionRequest

        public boolean isAttributeUnderAcquisitionRequest(int attribute)
        Returns true if the status for the designated attribute is REQUEST or REQUEST_AVAILABLE.

      • getAttributesReleasedToFederate

        public Set<Integer> getAttributesReleasedToFederate(int federateHandle)
        This method returns a set of all the attributes that have been released to the specified federate (that is, their status is AcquireRequest.Status.RELEASED and their associated federate is the same as the given handle. This call is for information only and has no lasting effect on the ownership data. If there are no attributes released to the federate, an empty set is returned.
